# pagewell

The PageWell skill for coding agents, and the CLI it
drives. An agent with this skill can write a do

cument that looks designed — an
article, a report, a handbook — or a single-page interactive
artifac

t, check it against the template's own rules, and publish it as a link:
a page of its own at `p.page

well.ai/s/…`, a share link, a share code, or a
single HTML file that opens offline.

`pagewell publish` defaults to a public, searchable page with its own stable
address. It does not cr

eate or join a visible Space unless you pass `--space`;
choose `--visibility unlisted|code|password`
for a restricted share instead.
## Install the skill

One command, any agent — it finds the agents on this machine and installs into
each of them:

`references/` next to i

t are what the agent loads on demand, and `assets/`
holds each template's screenshots and samples —

so clone
it into the directory your agent reads (`--depth 1`: the skill is a few
files; the history

You do not have to install the CLI yourself: the first time the agent needs it,
`SKILL.md` has it ru

n `scripts/install.sh`, which downloads the one binary
this machine needs from the `binaries` branch

and verifies it against
`SHA256SUMS` before putting it on your `PATH`. To do it now:

## DeepSeek Harness

This repository is also a DeepSeek Harness
(`dsh`) plugin: `package.json` declares a `dsh.bundle`, a

nd `dsh/index.js`
registers this same `SKILL.md` with dsh's skill registry. There is no second
copy
of the instructions, no build step and nothing to configure.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Or install `github:pagewellai/pagewell` from the Plugins page. The `pagewell` skill then
appears in

the agent's skill catalog: ask for an article, a page or a link, or
type `/pagewell`.

Installed the skill with `npx skills add pagewellai/pagewell -g` already? dsh reads
`~/.agents/skill

s` as well, so it has the skill without the plugin; with both,
dsh uses the `~/.agents/skills` copy.

Under dsh's default `workspace-write` sandbox, writing, checking, previewing,
exporting and publishi

ng run as they are. Signing in, `pagewell upgrade`,
installing the CLI and adding a template write t

o your home directory
(`~/.config/pagewell`, `~/.local/bin`, `~/.cache/pagewell`), so the agent
asks

to run that one command outside the sandbox: approve it in dsh, then
approve the device code in you

r browser. To update, run the command
`pagewell doctor` names (`dsh plugin --profile <profile> add g

ithub:pagewellai/pagewell`),
or update PageWell from the Plugins page.
## Updating
Every activation starts with a read-only check for both halves:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

If either half is behind, the JSON includes the exact next command. The manual
commands are:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Installed by `git clone` instead? `pagewell upgrade` fast-forwards that
clone and re-runs its instal

ler, so text and binary move together. Installed
with `npx skills`? `pagewell upgrade` swaps the bin

ary and reminds you to run
`npx skills update pagewell -g -y` for the text. A copy installed with th

e one-line
`curl` below has no skill on disk — `upgrade` then replaces the binary only
and says so.

You do not have to remember to check. The skill runs `doctor` before each
task and passes its own pu

blished version, so `update` covers the CLI and
`skill_update` covers SKILL.md plus its references.

Every later command that
talks to pagewell.ai also learns the current CLI version from the response;

a
newer one is mentioned once a day on stderr — never on stdout, so `--json`
stays clean. Set `PAGE
WELL_NO_UPDATE_NOTICE=1` to silence that later reminder.

Older versions keep working: the API only ever adds fields, and the server
never refuses a request b

ecause of the CLI's version. When a version is older
than the oldest one we still support, the remin

der becomes insistent (every
run, `update.required` in `doctor`) but nothing breaks.
## Releases

Every publish is a release with a semver tag, here and on
the source repository: `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH

`. A patch bump is fixes and text;
a minor bump adds commands, flags or fields; a major bump is rese

rved for the
day an old CLI genuinely cannot be served — there has been none. `main` is
always the l

atest release and `git checkout v0.3.1` gives you the skill text
published under that number. The bi

naries live on the `binaries` branch,
which always holds the current release only. What changed is i

n
`CHANGELOG.md`; where it came from is in `MANIFEST` and
`version.json`.
